html:
The Oglala are one of the seven bands of the Lakota, the western branch of the Sioux (Očhéthi Šakówiŋ, the Seven Council Fires). They moved west from the Missouri River onto the High Plains in the 1700s and, with horses, became bison hunters around the Black Hills and the Platte River.

Two of the most famous Lakota leaders were Oglala:

  • Red Cloud, who won the war of 1866 to 1868 over the Bozeman Trail and the Fort Laramie treaty of 1868;
  • Crazy Horse, a leader at the Battle of the Little Bighorn in 1876.

After the Black Hills were taken, most Oglala were settled on the Pine Ridge Reservation in South Dakota. There, in 1890, US troops killed some 250 to 300 Lakota at Wounded Knee. In 1973 activists occupied Wounded Knee for 71 days. The Oglala Sioux Tribe is one of the largest in the United States.
